title: Discovering Tut: the Saga Continues
subject: English

notes.heading: Theme
notes.text: The chapter explores how modern technology, forensic science, and archaeology come together to uncover long-buried historical secrets, mysteries of an ancient lineage, and the true cause of an unexpected royal demise.

summary: "Discovering Tut: The Saga Continues" by A.R. Williams provides a fascinating insight into the mystery surrounding the life and untimely demise of King Tutankhamun, the last teenage pharaoh of the powerful XVIII Dynasty that ruled Egypt for centuries. Discovered in 1922 by the British archaeologist Howard Carter, Tut's tomb was found packed with fabulous, glittering treasures of solid gold, making it the richest royal collection ever found. However, Carter's excavation sparked controversy because he had to chisel away the solidified ritual resins that cemented Tut's mummy to the bottom of his solid gold coffin, resulting in the body being severed at major joints to protect the treasure from thieves. The narrative shifts focus to modern forensic science in January 2005, when Tut’s mummy became the first to undergo a highly sophisticated CT scan using a portable scanner donated by National Geographic and Siemens. This scientific probe aimed to unravel the persistent mysteries surrounding his death at just 18 or 19 years of age, and to understand his exact royal lineage. The scan offered high-resolution, three-dimensional digital X-ray images, detailing his skull, neck vertebrae, and chest cage, proving that no vital parts were missing and dismissing earlier theories of foul play or a crushed breastbone suggested by an X-ray in 1968. The chapter also traces Tut's complex history, detailing how his grandfather Amenhotep III ruled during a golden age, followed by the eccentric Amenhotep IV (Akhenaten) who shocked Egypt by forcing the worship of Aten, changing the capital to Amarna, and smashing the images of the traditional god Amun. Tutankhamun restored the traditional ways, changing his name from Tutankhaten to honor Amun, before dying mysteriously after a brief nine-year reign. Ultimately, the CT scan provided relief to Zahi Hawass, the Secretary General of Egypt’s Supreme Council of Antiquities, as it showed the mummy was well-preserved, leaving King Tut to rest peacefully once more in his burial chamber under the watchful gaze of the Orion constellation.

qa.q: Give reasons why King Tut’s body has been subjected to repeated scrutiny.
qa.a: King Tut’s body has been examined repeatedly to discover the cause of his death and to learn more about his life and health.

qa.q: Give reasons why Howard Carter’s investigation was resented.
qa.a: Howard Carter’s investigation was resented because he damaged the mummy while trying to remove it from the coffin. The mummy had become stuck to the coffin due to hardened resins.

qa.q: Give reasons why Carter had to chisel away the solidified resins to raise the king’s remains.
qa.a: The resins had hardened and firmly stuck King Tut’s body to the bottom of the coffin. Carter had to chisel them away to remove the mummy.

qa.q: Give reasons why Tut’s body was buried along with gilded treasures.
qa.a: The Egyptians believed in life after death. They therefore buried their kings with valuable objects that they thought would be useful in the afterlife.

qa.q: Why was King Tut’s body buried with gilded treasures?
qa.a: King Tut was buried with gilded treasures because the ancient Egyptians believed that the dead continued to live in the afterlife. They believed that the king would need valuable objects and other possessions in his next life.

qa.q: What problems did Carter face when he examined Tut’s mummy?
qa.a: Carter found that the mummy was firmly stuck to the coffin because the resins used during burial had hardened. He had to use knives, a chisel and other tools to separate the body. In the process, the mummy was badly damaged.

qa.q: Why did scientists perform a CT scan on King Tut’s mummy?
qa.a: Scientists performed a CT scan to examine King Tut’s body without causing further damage. They wanted to learn about his physical condition, age and possible cause of death. The scan produced detailed images of his body.

qa.q: Scientific intervention is necessary to uncover the mysteries of the past. Do you agree?
qa.a: Yes, scientific intervention can help us understand the mysteries of the past. Modern technologies such as CT scans allow scientists to study ancient bodies without damaging them. They provide information about people, diseases, lifestyles and causes of death that may otherwise remain unknown.

qa.q: Advanced technology gives us new ways of studying ancient civilisations. What are some other examples?
qa.a: Advanced technology helps scientists study ancient civilisations through methods such as DNA testing, radiocarbon dating, satellite imaging and CT scanning. These techniques help reveal information about ancient people, their health, culture and way of life without destroying historical remains.

qa.q: What do you think are the reasons for the continued interest in King Tut?
qa.a: King Tut continues to attract interest because he became the Egyptian pharaoh at a very young age and died unexpectedly. His tomb contained many treasures and remained largely undisturbed for centuries. Modern scientific investigations have also created curiosity about his life and mysterious death.
